| Leftovers | Restores one sixteenth maximum HP at its residual recovery event. It cannot rescue a Pokémon already knocked out by an earlier event. |
| Choice Scarf | Multiplies effective Speed by 1.5 and applies its move lock; see M23. |
| Life Orb | Increases eligible attack damage by approximately 1.3 and normally causes one tenth maximum-HP recoil at its after-attack event. Sheer Force and Magic Guard interactions can change the recoil. |
| Air Balloon | Makes the holder ungrounded under ordinary conditions and pops on an applicable damaging hit. Ordinary residual chip does not automatically pop it. |
| Iron Ball | Halves Speed and grounds the holder. Its interaction with the Flying type's Ground immunity has dedicated handling; do not infer every dual-type damage result solely from the word “grounded.” |
| Light Clay | Extends a newly established relevant screen from five to eight turns. |
| Damp Rock / Heat Rock / Smooth Rock / Icy Rock | Extend newly established rain/sun/sandstorm/snow from five to eight turns. |
| Terrain Extender | Extends newly established terrain from five to eight turns. |
| Eject Button — Champions | After an eligible damaging move, can be consumed to switch the surviving holder to a chosen available reserve. It checks competing switch flags and other blocking conditions in the Champions override. |
| Red Card | After an eligible hit, can be consumed to force the surviving attacker toward a random eligible reserve under its own restrictions. It does not let the holder freely choose the opponent's replacement. |
| King's Rock | Adds its qualifying flinch chance to eligible attacks that do not already carry a flinch chance. Action order and flinch prevention remain relevant. |
| Compatible Mega Stone | Enables its specified Mega form when eligible. It has special removal and transfer restrictions when held by a compatible species. |

Damage-triggered switches, pivot moves, survival effects, berries, and secondary effects can compete at different moments. Read an Eject Button or Red Card interaction together with the move and the relevant ability, particularly Sheer Force or an automatic switch ability. The library does not assert a universal “every trigger activates” rule.

Trick and Switcheroo exchange items subject to their failure conditions. A compatible Mega Stone has transfer protection in the Champions definitions. Removing an item, consuming it, suppressing it, and changing its holder have different consequences.

M28.text:
# Special damage and multi-hit attacks

Fixed and reactive damage, OHKO rules, variable hit counts, between-hit triggers, and self-damage families.

## Reference text

Include the relevant family when a considered move uses it. Dependencies: exact move definition, immunity, Substitute, contact/secondary events, HP history.

Fixed-damage moves and HP-setting effects do not use the ordinary power/offense/defense formula. Seismic Toss-style level damage, Super Fang's current-HP fraction, Final Gambit's use of the attacker's current HP, and Pain Split's HP averaging are different mechanisms. Their own type immunities, failure checks, and Substitute interactions still matter.

Counter-like attacks depend on a qualifying earlier hit in the same turn. Counter uses qualifying physical damage, Mirror Coat uses qualifying special damage, and Metal Burst has its own broader rule and multiplier. The target may be the last qualifying attacker rather than the originally preferred foe. Only the relevant last hit, not necessarily the entire total of a multi-hit attack, supplies their damage history.

One-hit knockout moves use special accuracy, level, and immunity rules. They are not guaranteed knockouts merely because their effect is called “one-hit KO,” and increasing ordinary offensive stats does not turn them into ordinary high-power attacks. Sturdy and move-specific type immunities can stop them.

For ordinary attacks with a variable two-to-five hit count, the hit-count distribution is 35% for two, 35% for three, 15% for four, and 15% for five, before modifying effects. Skill Link can change this. Other multi-hit moves can have a fixed count or individual accuracy checks.

Each hit can interact with Substitute, full-HP protection, contact reactions, berries, and current HP. Exact HP-threshold timing for Anger Shell and Berserk during multi-hit attacks is uncertain.

Recoil, crash damage, self-KO, and HP costs are separate categories. A missed ordinary recoil move does not necessarily behave like a missed jump-kick-style crash move. An Explosion-style self-KO does not require the same conditions as Final Gambit. Use the actual move's rule rather than a generic “self damage” label.

M30.text:
# Selected end-of-turn ordering

Selected end-of-turn event order, recovery before or after damage, expiry, suborders, and fainting limits.

## Reference text

Include when multiple residual effects, recovery, expiry, or delayed events are relevant. Dependencies: current effect counters, active Pokémon, ability/item suppression, fainting.

This table lists selected end-of-turn effects. Earlier applicable events resolve first; an effect can expire before its next activation. Events in the same family can have additional ordering by suborder and holder.

| Relative order | Selected effects |
| ---: | --- |
| 1 | Weather duration/processing and weather-triggered events. |
| 3 | Future attack resolution. |
| 4 | Wish. |
| 5 | Selected passive effects: Grassy Terrain recovery at suborder 2, Healer at suborder 3, Leftovers at suborder 4. |
| 6–7 | Aqua Ring, then Ingrain recovery. |
| 8 | Leech Seed. |
| 9 | Poison or bad poison. |
| 10 | Burn. |
| 11–12 | Nightmare, then Curse. |
| 13–14 | Binding/Salt Cure, then effects such as Octolock. |
| 15–17 | Taunt, Encore, Disable duration processing. |
| 23 | Yawn. |
| 24 | Perish Song. |
| 26 | Side-condition duration processing, including screens and Tailwind, with their own suborders. |
| 27 | Field-condition duration processing, including Trick Room, Gravity, other rooms, and terrain. |
| 28 and later | Selected late ability/item updates such as Speed Boost or Harvest; other late effects are possible. |

The numbers indicate ordering, not turn counts or priority brackets for chosen moves. A Pokémon can faint before its next listed recovery opportunity. Grassy Terrain's recovery occurs before its later terrain-duration expiration step; weather uses different event placement. Do not apply one generic expiration rule to every effect.

For shared-order events or simultaneous knockouts, preserve the engine's actual event history. A request without enough information to resolve a fine timing interaction does not justify inventing an exact result.

interaction:psychic-terrain-priority.text:
# Psychic Terrain and opposing priority

`interaction:psychic-terrain-priority` · Grounded targets, positive priority, and side identity determine this protection.

## When to retrieve

Psychic Terrain is active or may be set, and a contemplated attack has positive effective priority.

## Conditional rule

Psychic Terrain blocks opposing positive-priority moves against grounded targets. Test the target’s grounding and the move’s effective priority when it would hit. The user’s own grounding is not the condition for this protection.

## Exceptions and required state

It does not block ally-targeted moves by this rule, nor protect an airborne target. This terrain protection does not apply to self-targeted moves or semi-invulnerable targets; those have separate hit checks. Abilities and other effects can change grounding or priority.

interaction:dark-prankster.text:
# Dark typing and Prankster

`interaction:dark-prankster` · A Dark target can reject a Prankster-boosted opposing move.

## When to retrieve

An opposing Prankster user may aim a status move at a Dark-type Pokémon.

## Conditional rule

Dark types are immune to opposing moves boosted by Prankster. This is a separate check from ordinary type effectiveness and Psychic Terrain.

## Exceptions and required state

A move affecting the field or the user’s own side is not thereby an attack aimed at the Dark Pokémon. Ally targeting is exempt from this immunity. Check current typing and whether the ability actually modified this move.

interaction:ability-priority-protection.text:
# Armor Tail and Queenly Majesty

`interaction:ability-priority-protection` · Active ability holders can protect their side from opposing priority.

## When to retrieve

One of these abilities is active and a positive-priority opposing move may target its side.

## Conditional rule

These abilities can block opposing positive-priority moves aimed at the holder or its allies. Unlike Psychic Terrain’s protection, the ability rule does not require the protected target to be grounded.

## Exceptions and required state

The holder must be active and the ability effective at that moment. Suppression and applicable ability-ignoring effects matter. It is not a general immunity to all moves or a guarantee against a move whose final priority is nonpositive.

interaction:guards-and-target-shape.text:
# Wide Guard, Quick Guard, and target shape

`interaction:guards-and-target-shape` · Side protection depends on spread targeting or positive priority.

## When to retrieve

A side may use Wide Guard or Quick Guard before an incoming move.

## Conditional rule

Wide Guard protects its side against eligible moves whose target is all adjacent Pokémon or all adjacent foes, including an ally’s spread move. Quick Guard protects its side from eligible positive-priority moves. Their repeat-use rules differ from ordinary Protect: they update the shared protection counter but do not use it as their own failure roll.

## Exceptions and required state

Use the move’s actual target/priority and protection eligibility, and check protection bypass. Wide Guard is not inferred solely from how many targets remain; a spread-target move can still qualify with only one target present.

interaction:contact-through-protection.text:
# Champions contact damage through protection

`interaction:contact-through-protection` · Unseen Fist and Piercing Drill can permit quarter damage through protection.

## When to retrieve

A contact move from a holder of effective Unseen Fist or Piercing Drill encounters protection.

## Conditional rule

The Champions protection hook marks eligible contact hits as bypassing protection. The damage engine then applies a 0.25 damage modifier for that bypass. Do not import the older assumption that Unseen Fist always deals full damage through Protect.

## Exceptions and required state

This requires an effective ability and contact flag at the relevant check. It does not grant universal success against immunities, accuracy failure, or every other defensive effect. Protection-specific side effects and hit processing still require their own rules.

interaction:intimidate-and-stat-response.text:
# Intimidate and stat-drop responses

`interaction:intimidate-and-stat-responses` · A switch-in Attack drop can fail or trigger a retaliatory boost.

## When to retrieve

An effective Intimidate user enters, or an opposing stat drop may reach a Defiant or Competitive holder.

## Conditional rule

Intimidate attempts to lower opposing Attack by one stage. Substitute and applicable stat-drop/Intimidate immunity can prevent the drop. When an opposing Pokémon actually lowers a stat stage, Defiant can raise Attack by two stages and Competitive can raise Special Attack by two stages.

## Exceptions and required state

Check current abilities, suppression, stat limits, substitute, and whether a drop actually occurred. Defiant/Competitive are not triggered simply by seeing the opponent’s species. Their triggers concern opposing-caused drops, not ordinary self-caused drops.

interaction:powder-redirection.text:
# Rage Powder, Follow Me, and powder immunity

`interaction:powder-redirection` · Redirection eligibility depends on move shape, actor immunity, and active effects.

## When to retrieve

An active Follow Me or Rage Powder user may attract a targeted move.

## Conditional rule

Follow Me and Rage Powder redirect eligible opposing single-target moves while their effect is active. Rage Powder is subject to powder immunity: a Grass-type attacker or an attacker with effective Overcoat ignores that powder-based redirection. Follow Me does not inherit that powder exception.

## Exceptions and required state

Spread moves are not converted into single-target moves by redirection. Check the move’s targeting and any redirection-ignoring ability or move rule. Safety Goggles is not admitted in this pinned Champions item catalogue and must not be assumed available.

interaction:sound-and-substitute.text:
# Sound moves and Substitute

`interaction:sound-and-substitute` · A bypass flag and sound immunity are different checks.

## When to retrieve

A contemplated sound move faces a Substitute or Soundproof holder.

## Conditional rule

Moves carrying the bypasssub flag can affect the Pokémon behind a Substitute instead of being absorbed by that substitute. Many sound moves carry this flag. Soundproof can separately prevent applicable sound moves from affecting its holder.

## Exceptions and required state

Inspect the actual resolved move flags; do not infer all exceptions from a name or animation. Bypassing Substitute does not bypass Soundproof, typing, accuracy, or protection automatically. Ability suppression or an applicable ability-ignoring move changes the Soundproof check.

interaction:seed-and-unburden.text:
# Terrain Seeds and Unburden

`interaction:seed-and-unburden` · Item consumption and terrain activation can change both bulk and Speed.

## When to retrieve

A terrain seed holder with Unburden may enter matching terrain or have matching terrain set.

## Conditional rule

An effective matching Terrain Seed consumes itself when its activation conditions are met and raises the corresponding defensive stat. Effective Unburden can double Speed after the held item is lost or consumed. This can change the remaining action order.

## Exceptions and required state

A Pokémon merely starting without an item does not automatically receive the boost. Check actual consumption, item suppression, stat limits, active ability, switch history, and whether a new item has been gained. The seed trigger itself does not require the holder to be grounded.

interaction:white-herb-and-unburden.text:
# White Herb, stat drops, and Unburden

`interaction:white-herb-and-unburden` · A consumed White Herb can remove negative stages and activate Unburden.

## When to retrieve

A White Herb holder may acquire negative stat stages, especially when it has Unburden.

## Conditional rule

When its activation conditions are met, White Herb restores the holder’s negative stat stages to zero and is consumed. The resulting item loss can activate effective Unburden. Positive stages are not reset by this item.

## Exceptions and required state

Check that negative stages exist, the item can activate, and consumption actually occurs. Do not assume every intended stat drop succeeds or that a previously consumed Herb remains available. New item acquisition and switching affect Unburden state.

interaction:weather-speed.text:
# Weather abilities and Speed order

`interaction:weather-speed` · Weather-dependent Speed changes interact with Trick Room and suppression.

## When to retrieve

Rain, sun, sandstorm, or snow can activate a relevant Speed ability.

## Conditional rule

Swift Swim, Chlorophyll, Sand Rush, and Slush Rush double their holder’s Speed in their corresponding effective weather. Trick Room reverses the Speed comparison within the same priority bracket; a faster Pokémon can therefore act later under it.

## Exceptions and required state

Check active weather, weather suppression, effective ability, stat stages, and other Speed modifiers. Weather does not change move priority by this mechanism. Champions Trick Room has no older extreme-Speed wraparound.

interaction:grounding-and-ground-immunit.text:
# Grounding and Ground-type immunity

`interaction:grounding-and-ground-immunity` · Flying, Levitate, and forced grounding require separate checks.

## When to retrieve

A Ground move, terrain effect, Gravity, or a grounding-changing effect may matter.

## Conditional rule

Flying typing normally supplies a type-chart Ground immunity. Effective Levitate supplies an ability-based Ground immunity. Gravity and other grounding effects can remove relevant airborne protections. Ordinary Ground attacks should use the target’s current grounding and the specific immunity source.

## Exceptions and required state

A Mold Breaker-style bypass can ignore an applicable ability immunity without removing Flying typing. Move-specific exceptions require their own definitions. Iron Ball, Air Balloon, Magnet Rise, and semi-invulnerability are not interchangeable flags.

interaction:freeze-dry-water.text:
# Freeze-Dry and Water typing

`interaction:freeze-dry-water` · A move-specific effectiveness override is not ordinary Ice coverage.

## When to retrieve

Freeze-Dry may hit a Water-type target.

## Conditional rule

Freeze-Dry sets its effectiveness against the Water component to super effective. Combine that factor with the target’s other current type component and remaining modifiers. The Champions move has no secondary freeze chance.

## Exceptions and required state

This is not a general rule for all Ice moves and does not remove independent accuracy, protection, or ability checks. If another effect changes the move’s type, account for its effective type and the resulting effectiveness rule.

interaction:grassy-glide-priority.text:
# Grassy Glide and terrain-dependent priority

`interaction:grassy-glide-priority` · A move can gain priority only under its actual terrain conditions.

## When to retrieve

Grassy Glide is considered while Grassy Terrain is present or might be replaced.

## Conditional rule

Grassy Glide gains one priority level when its user is affected by Grassy Terrain. Grounding and the currently effective terrain therefore matter to move order and priority-blocking effects.

## Exceptions and required state

Do not permanently encode it as a +1 move. Terrain can be changed before execution, and the engine’s ordering/priority events decide the relevant timing. Check current user grounding and all other priority modifiers.

interaction:upper-hand-eligibility.text:
# Upper Hand and pending priority attacks

`interaction:upper-hand-eligibility` · Upper Hand depends on the target’s still-pending action.

## When to retrieve

Upper Hand may be used against a possible positive-priority attack.

## Conditional rule

Upper Hand has base priority +3. It fails unless the target still has a pending damaging move with positive effective priority. Its flinch effect matters only if the hit succeeds and the target can flinch before acting.

## Exceptions and required state

Protect, a switch, an ordinary nonpriority move, a status move, or a target that already acted does not satisfy that eligibility check. At equal priority, Speed and ties can decide whether the target has already acted. Type immunity and flinch immunity are separate checks.

interaction:sash-and-multiple-hits.text:
# Focus Sash and multiple hits

`interaction:sash-and-multiple-hits` · Full-HP survival is evaluated for the hit that would cause fainting.

## When to retrieve

Focus Sash is known or plausible, particularly against a multi-hit attack or residual damage.

## Conditional rule

An effective Focus Sash can let a full-HP holder survive a damaging attack’s otherwise fatal hit at 1 HP and is consumed. Later hits of a multi-hit move can still knock out the holder. Damage taken earlier can remove the full-HP condition.

## Exceptions and required state

This is not a universal guarantee to survive a turn. Track current HP, item presence/suppression, the order of hits, and damage that is not eligible for the item trigger. Do not invent exact HP from rounded opponent percentages.

interaction:contact-and-helmet.text:
# Contact and Rocky Helmet

`interaction:contact-and-helmet` · Damage category does not determine whether a move makes contact.

## When to retrieve

An effective Rocky Helmet holder may be hit by a contact move.

## Conditional rule

Rocky Helmet responds to qualifying contact hits by damaging the attacker for one sixth of its maximum HP. A multi-hit contact move can trigger the effect for multiple hits. Contact is a move flag, not a synonym for Physical category.

## Exceptions and required state

Check actual contact at the hit event: Long Reach and other effects can prevent contact behavior. Item suppression, substitute routing, and effects that prevent indirect damage can change the result. Do not charge recoil merely because the attacker selected a contact move that failed to connect.

interaction:encore-queued-priority.text:
# Champions Encore and queued priority

`interaction:encore-queued-priority` · Encore can replace a pending move and change its priority.

## When to retrieve

Encore may land before the target executes a different selected move.

## Conditional rule

When the last move is eligible, Encore forces repetition under its duration and PP rules. Encore can replace a pending move and adjust its priority by the difference between the old and repeated move’s base priorities.

## Exceptions and required state

Check last move, eligibility flags, PP, whether an action remains queued, and Mental Herb. Mental Herb’s effect on the pending move’s priority is uncertain.

interaction:mega-form-state.text:
# Mega Evolution and current form state

`interaction:mega-form-state` · Starting ability, transformation eligibility, and current Mega ability are distinct.

## When to retrieve

A Pokémon holds a compatible Mega Stone or has already Mega Evolved.

## Conditional rule

A compatible stone enables the corresponding transformation when the side still has its permitted Mega Evolution. The resulting form has its own types, base statistics, and ability. Keep the starting set and current form separate. Champions keeps the Mega form after withdrawal and fainting.

## Exceptions and required state

Holding a stone does not prove transformation occurred. A team can carry several stones but use only one Mega Evolution per battle. A known Mega ability does not identify an unknown starting ability. The resulting form after Revival Blessing is uncertain.

interaction:terrain-status-prevention.text:
# Terrain and status prevention

`interaction:terrain-status-prevention` · Groundedness and the timing of status application determine prevention.

## When to retrieve

Electric or Misty Terrain is present or might be set before a status attempt.

## Conditional rule

Electric Terrain prevents applicable sleep attempts against affected grounded Pokémon. Misty Terrain prevents applicable major-status and confusion attempts against affected grounded Pokémon. These are prevention rules, not automatic cures of an already established status.

## Exceptions and required state

Check current grounding, effective terrain, the actual status-application event, and move-specific exceptions. Yawn’s delayed sleep is evaluated when sleep would be applied, so the terrain at that later point matters.

ability:auraguard.text:
# Aura Guard

Damage received from moves with the contact flag is multiplied by 0.5. Apply this to the current holder while the ability is active.

Uncertain interaction: whether ability-bypass effects ignore Aura Guard.
